questions.question: Define osmosis.
questions.modelAnswer: The net movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.
markingPoints: The net movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.question: Explain what happens to a plant cell placed in a dilute solution.
questions.modelAnswer: Water enters by osmosis; the vacuole/cytoplasm swells; the cell becomes turgid because the cell wall resists further expansion.
markingPoints: Water enters by osmosis
the vacuole/cytoplasm swells
the cell becomes turgid because the cell wall resists further expansion.

questions.question: Explain why an animal cell may burst in a very dilute solution but a plant cell normally does not.
questions.modelAnswer: Water enters both cells by osmosis; an animal cell has no cell wall so its membrane may rupture; a plant cell wall supports the cell and resists the pressure.
markingPoints: Water enters both cells by osmosis
an animal cell has no cell wall so its membrane may rupture
a plant cell wall supports the cell and resists the pressure.

questions.question: A potato cylinder changes from 4.0 g to 4.6 g. Calculate the percentage change in mass.
questions.modelAnswer: percentage change = (change ÷ original value) × 100. ((4.6 − 4.0) ÷ 4.0) × 100 = 15% increase. Answer: ((4.6 − 4.0) ÷ 4.0) × 100 = 15% increase.

questions.question: Define active transport.
questions.modelAnswer: The movement of substances from a lower concentration to a higher concentration, against the concentration gradient, using energy from respiration.
markingPoints: The movement of substances from a lower concentration to a higher concentration, against the concentration gradient, using energy from respiration.

questions.question: Explain why mineral ions enter root hair cells by active transport rather than diffusion.
questions.modelAnswer: Mineral-ion concentration can be lower in the soil than in root cells; movement is against the concentration gradient; energy from respiration is required.
markingPoints: Mineral-ion concentration can be lower in the soil than in root cells
movement is against the concentration gradient
energy from respiration is required.

questions.question: Explain how glucose can be absorbed from the small intestine when its concentration is lower in the intestine than in the blood.
questions.modelAnswer: Glucose is moved against its concentration gradient by active transport using energy from respiration.

questions.question: Compare diffusion, osmosis and active transport.
questions.modelAnswer: Diffusion: net movement of particles from high to low concentration , passive/no energy required . Osmosis: net movement of water only through a partially permeable membrane from dilute to concentrated solution . Active transport: moves substances from low to high concentration / against the gradient , requiring energy from respiration .
markingPoints: Diffusion: net movement of particles from high to low concentration , passive/no energy required . Osmosis: net movement of water only through a partially permeable membrane from dilute to concentrated solution . Active transport: moves substances from low to high concentration / against the gradient , requiring energy from respiration .
